_note: Starter records for a tinnitus knowledge graph. Every quote was copied from the linked source on 2026-10-31 and is kept under 15 words. agentType is automated_agent until a person approves each relationship. Not medical advice.

records.name: Tinnitus
records.tldr: Hearing a sound such as ringing, buzzing or hissing when no outside sound is present.

sources.label: Clinical practice guideline: Tinnitus (Tunkel et al., 2014)
Human Phenotype Ontology term for tinnitus

records.name: Hearing impairment
records.tldr: Reduced ability to hear sound; hearing-related factors are among the few tinnitus risk factors with supporting evidence.

sources.label: Low evidence for tinnitus risk factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Biswas et al., 2023)
Human Phenotype Ontology term for hearing impairment

relations.quote: positive causal associations were found for various hearing-related factors

records.name: Cognitive behavioural therapy for tinnitus
records.tldr: A talking therapy that changes how a person thinks about and reacts to tinnitus, rather than removing the sound.

sources.label: Cognitive behavioural therapy for tinnitus (Cochrane review, Fuller et al., 2020)
Medical Action Ontology (MAXO): term MAXO:0000883, cognitive behavior therapy

relations.quote: reducing the negative impact that tinnitus can have on quality of life

records.name: Sound therapy with hearing aids or sound generators
records.tldr: Devices that amplify outside sound or add background sound; a 2018 review found they may make little or no difference to tinnitus severity, on low-certainty evidence.

sources.label: Sound therapy (using amplification devices or sound generators) for tinnitus (Cochrane review, Sereda et al., 2018)

relations.quote: might result in little or no difference in tinnitus symptom severity

closeMatches.label: hearing aid usage
closeMatches.note: covers hearing aids only, not sound generators; not an exact match

records.name: Bimodal neuromodulation (sound plus tongue stimulation)
records.tldr: Pairs sounds played through headphones with mild electrical pulses to the tongue, aiming to retrain how the brain processes sound.

sources.label: Bimodal neuromodulation combining sound and tongue stimulation reduces tinnitus symptoms (Conlon et al., 2020)

relations.quote: participants achieved a statistically significant reduction in tinnitus symptom severity

closeMatches.label: stimulation procedure
closeMatches.note: much broader parent term; no exact MAXO term exists yet

records.name: Lenire
records.tldr: A commercial bimodal neuromodulation device for tinnitus; the FDA classified it as a class II device through the De Novo pathway on 6 March 2023.

sources.label: FDA final order: classification of the combined acoustic and electrical external stimulation device for the relief of tinnitus (Federal Register, Docket FDA-2026-N-6010)

relations.quote: On March 6, 2023, FDA issued an order to the requester classifying the device into class II.
a combined acoustic and electrical intraoral stimulation device for the relief of tinnitus

records.name: Neuromod Devices
records.tldr: Dublin-based company that makes the Lenire tinnitus treatment device.

records.name: Treatment Evaluation of Neuromodulation for Tinnitus (TENT-A)
records.tldr: Randomised, triple-blind exploratory trial in Ireland and Germany comparing three bimodal stimulation settings over 12 weeks.

sources.label: Bi-modal stimulation in the treatment of tinnitus: study protocol (BMJ Open, 2017)

relations.quote: Bi-modal stimulation in the treatment of tinnitus

records.name: Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI)
records.tldr: A self-report questionnaire that scores how much tinnitus affects daily life.

sources.label: Development of the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (Newman, Jacobson and Spitzer, 1996)

relations.quote: The total scale yielded excellent internal consistency reliability

records.name: Clinical practice guideline: Tinnitus (AAO-HNSF, 2014)
records.tldr: US clinical guideline that recommends cognitive behavioural therapy for persistent, bothersome tinnitus and hearing aid evaluation when hearing loss is present.

sources.label: Clinical practice guideline: Tinnitus (Tunkel et al., 2014)
ASHA Evidence Maps summary of the 2014 tinnitus guideline
